questions.question: A developer works on a computer that does not have Docker installed. The developer needs to build the Dockerfile in the current folder and push the image to the registry contosoacr as ragapi:v1. Which command should the developer run?

options.text: az acr build --registry contosoacr --image ragapi:v1 .
options.why: Correct. az acr build runs a quick task that builds in Azure and pushes the image to the registry.

options.text: docker build -t contosoacr.azurecr.io/ragapi:v1 .
options.why: This requires Docker on the local computer.

options.text: az acr import --name contosoacr --image ragapi:v1
options.why: az acr import copies existing images. It does not build from a Dockerfile.

options.text: az acr repository update --name contosoacr --image ragapi:v1
options.why: This changes image attributes. It does not build an image.

questions.explanation: Quick tasks run the build in Azure, so no local Docker engine is required.

questions.question: You must configure Azure Container Registry to rebuild an application image automatically when its base image, python:3.12-slim, receives a security update. What should you configure?

options.text: An ACR task with a base image update trigger
options.why: Correct. The base image update trigger reruns the task when the image in the FROM instruction is updated.

options.text: A webhook that fires on image push to your registry
options.why: A webhook on your own registry does not detect updates to an upstream base image or run a build.

options.text: Geo-replication for the registry
options.why: Geo-replication replicates images across regions and does not rebuild images.

options.text: A retention policy for untagged manifests
options.why: A retention policy deletes old manifests and does not rebuild images.

questions.explanation: ACR Tasks can trigger on base image updates to keep application images patched.

questions.question: You run the following command to create an ACR task: az acr task create --registry contosoacr --name build-api --image api:{{.Run.ID}} --context https://github.com/contoso/api.git#main --file Dockerfile --git-access-token $GITHUB_PAT. Which TWO events will start the task by default?

options.text: A commit is pushed to the main branch of the repository
options.why: Correct. The source code commit trigger is enabled by default for tasks with a Git context.

options.text: The base image referenced in the Dockerfile is updated
options.why: Correct. The base image update trigger is enabled by default.

options.text: A user pulls the api image from the registry
options.why: Image pulls do not trigger tasks.

options.text: The registry SKU is changed
options.why: Changing the SKU does not trigger tasks.

questions.explanation: By default, a task with a Git context runs on source code commits and on base image updates. A schedule must be added explicitly.

questions.question: You need a single ACR task definition that builds an image, runs unit tests inside the built container, and pushes the image only if the tests succeed. What should you create?

options.text: A multi-step task defined in a YAML file with build, cmd, and push steps
options.why: Correct. Multi-step tasks run steps in order, so a failing cmd step stops the run before the push step.

options.text: A quick task started with az acr build
options.why: A quick task builds and pushes, but it does not run a separate test step.

options.text: A scheduled task with a timer trigger
options.why: A timer controls when a task runs, not which steps it runs.

options.text: A repository-scoped token
options.why: Tokens control registry access and do not define build steps.

questions.explanation: Multi-step tasks defined in YAML support build, test and push workflows.

questions.question: In the az acr task create command, what is the purpose of the --context parameter?

options.text: It specifies the location of the source code, such as a Git repository URL and branch
options.why: Correct. The context is the source location that the task builds from.

options.text: It specifies the name of the image to push
options.why: The image name is specified by the --image parameter.

options.text: It specifies the Azure region in which the task runs
options.why: Tasks run in the region of the registry. --context does not set a region.

options.text: It specifies the subscription that is billed for the task
options.why: Billing follows the registry's subscription.

questions.explanation: --context points to the source, and --file names the Dockerfile or YAML file within it.
